name: Book collection centre appointments online
sector: health care: medical laboratory testing and health services
summary: Patients who need blood or urine collected can book a time at one of about 200 collection centres instead of queuing as walk-ins. Most book themselves on the website, which reserves a slot, sends a confirmation and a reminder and puts the booked patient ahead of walk-ins on arrival; about one in ten books by phone through the contact centre, including timed tests that need the centre to confirm staff and equipment. Booking is almost all automatic, but cancellations, no-shows, unexpected centre closures, duplicate bookings and patients whose confirmations never arrive create work for contact centre and digital support staff and leave slots empty while walk-ins wait.

baseline.org_archetype: A large Canadian community laboratory company with about 200 collection centres in Ontario, Quebec and Manitoba, an online booking tool, a patient portal and a central contact centre.
baseline.notes: Online booking grew sharply from 2020 when centres limited walk-ins for physical distancing; requisition upload started in September 2020. The current MyTurn tool is later than the period and is used only as evidence of common booking rules.

trigger: A patient asks for a collection centre time slot online or by phone.
end_state: The patient has arrived and is in the centre's registration queue, or the booking ended as a cancellation, a no-show, a centre closure or an attempt that never became a booking.

volume.seasonality: Follows collection visits: busiest on weekday mornings and in January, quieter in July, August and late December; booking share rose in 2020 and 2021.

evidence.note: Taken from the organisation file's process map (driver d_psc_visits, about 57% of visits booked), itself an estimate.

Wage from Job Bank (cost in the organisation file is wage times 1.35). FTE is the author's estimate: about 10% of bookings made by phone at 3 to 8 minutes, plus calls about existing bookings and closure rebooking; the contact centre has 110 representatives.
Estimate: web and email booking problems for about 1% of bookings and daily duplicate clean-up; the organisation file's portal workflow already uses 7 of the 14 agents.

roles.title: Collection centre team lead
roles.department: Laboratory and Health Services Centres network

evidence.note: Estimate: confirming about 2,000 special-test phone bookings a month and closing schedules for unplanned closures; the organisation file's other workflows use 20 of the 55 team leads.

systems.name: Online appointment booking and centre queue management
The consumer health service patient portal and online test shop
Contact centre telephony with IVR, queues and call recording
CRM for client accounts, sales pipeline and service cases

steps.name: Patient starts a booking
steps.description: The patient, usually holding a requisition from their clinician, opens the location finder on the company website and chooses to book, or phones the customer care line because they prefer to talk to someone or need a special test.

evidence.note: Online booking from the location finder (dyn_findloc) and phone booking of special tests (dyn_before); the 90 to 10 channel split is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Patient picks the centre, visit type and time slot
steps.description: On the booking page the patient filters centres by distance, opens one, chooses the visit type (routine blood and urine, or a timed test) and picks one of the open slots shown for the coming days. Patient time of two to five minutes is not counted as staff work.

error.defect_description: Patient picks the wrong visit type or centre, for example a routine slot for a two-hour glucose test.

next.condition: no convenient slot, patient walks in or goes elsewhere
error or confusion, patient contacts digital support

evidence.note: Shares are the author's estimates; slot availability was tighter in 2020 and 2021 when centres reduced capacity for distancing.

steps.name: Patient enters contact details and answers screening questions
steps.description: The patient types name, date of birth, phone number and email and agrees to receive notices; in 2020 to 2022 the form also asked COVID-19 screening questions and told symptomatic patients not to book.

error.defect_description: Typo in the phone number or email, so notices do not arrive.

control.basis: Ontario Personal Health Information Protection Act: consent and limited collection for contact details; COVID-19 screening of visitors under provincial public health direction (2020 to 2022)

next.condition: screened out or abandons the form

evidence.note: Screening practice in 2020 to 2022 and the shares are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Booking system reserves the slot and sends the confirmation
steps.description: The booking engine holds the slot, adds the patient to the centre's appointment list and sends a confirmation email and text with the address, preparation notes and links to cancel or reschedule.

evidence.note: Confirmation with reschedule and cancel links (dyn_myturn, a later version of the tool); portal users can keep track of appointments (dyn_plus); upload share is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Customer care representative books by phone
steps.description: After the telephone queue, a representative confirms the patient's identity, checks the test and any preparation rules, searches open slots at the centres the patient can reach, books the slot in the appointment system and reads back the time, address and preparation instructions.

error.defect_description: Wrong phone number or email keyed, so reminders do not arrive.

next.condition: special test needs the centre to confirm

evidence.note: Special tests booked by contacting the centre (dyn_before); handle and queue times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Patient uploads the requisition in advance
steps.description: The patient photographs the requisition and submits it with the physician's and patient's names and date of birth through the upload page; requisitions older than six months are refused, and a confirmation email follows.

error.defect_description: Blurred image or missing page, so the centre still needs the paper copy.

control.basis: Company upload rule: requisitions older than six months are not accepted

evidence.note: Upload fields, the six-month rule and the confirmation email are stated (dyn_upload); started September 2020.

steps.name: File the uploaded requisition for the centre
steps.description: The upload service stores the image in the requisition imaging system, where centre staff can find it by patient name and date of birth when the patient arrives.

error.defect_description: Image filed under a misspelled name and not found at registration.

evidence.note: Patient tells staff on arrival that the requisition was uploaded (dyn_upload).

steps.name: Hold the booking until the reminder is due
steps.description: The appointment sits on the centre's schedule until the day before; most patients book for the next few days, and some book weeks ahead for timed tests or a preferred centre.

evidence.note: Appointments can be booked up to 4 weeks ahead (dyn_myturn); the lead time distribution is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Send the reminder
steps.description: The booking system sends a reminder text or email the day before with the time, address, preparation reminder and the cancel and reschedule links.

evidence.note: Reminder timing and shares are the author's estimates; reminders reduce no-shows only modestly (kheirkhah2016 found a small effect for phone reminders).

steps.name: Patient cancels or reschedules
steps.description: The patient uses the link to cancel or move the appointment, or phones in; a moved booking goes back to slot selection and the freed slot reappears in the calendar.

evidence.note: Reschedule and cancel links (dyn_myturn); shares are estimates.

steps.name: Team lead closes the centre's schedule
steps.description: When staff call in sick, the building loses power or a storm closes roads, the collection centre team lead blocks the affected slots in the booking system, marks the centre closed on the location finder and sends the list of booked patients to the contact centre.

error.defect_description: Some booked patients left off the list and arrive at a closed centre.

evidence.note: Unexpected closures flagged on the location finder (dyn_findloc); per-booking time is the team lead's time per closure divided by the bookings affected.

steps.name: Patient arrives for the appointment or does not
steps.description: On the day the patient comes to the centre at the booked time and tells the front desk; patients who come more than 15 minutes late are seen as walk-ins, and some do not come at all.

evidence.note: Arrival and 15-minute hold rule (dyn_myturn); outpatient no-show rates of 12.6% to 25.7% (kheirkhah2016); 10% is the author's estimate for short-notice laboratory visits.

steps.name: Mark the arrival and pass the patient to the centre queue
steps.description: The booking system shows the patient as arrived when the lab assistant checks them in, and the booked visit moves ahead of walk-ins in the centre's queue for registration.

evidence.note: Pre-booked patients prioritised (dyn_myturn); community laboratories averaged 14 to 17 minutes from arrival to service (ag2017).

steps.name: Release the slot and record a no-show
steps.description: Fifteen minutes after the booked time the system releases the unused slot and records the absence, which feeds the centre's no-show statistics; the patient may later walk in or rebook.

control.basis: Booking rule: a booked slot is held up to 15 minutes past the appointment time

evidence.note: Hold rule stated for the current tool (dyn_myturn).

steps.name: Digital support agent resolves a booking problem
steps.description: A support agent picks up the patient's web form or email during office hours, verifies the patient's identity, looks up the booking, then resends a missing confirmation, corrects the contact details or books the slot for the patient.

error.defect_description: Booking details disclosed without enough identity checks.

control.basis: Ontario Personal Health Information Protection Act: verify identity before discussing a patient's booking

next.condition: booking existed, confirmation resent or details fixed
patient gives up or walks in

evidence.note: Support works office hours, so requests wait about a day; shares are estimates.

steps.name: Contact centre notifies patients of a closure and rebooks
steps.description: A representative texts or phones each patient on the closure list, offers another slot at a nearby centre or another day, and books it, or tells the patient to walk in elsewhere.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Customer care representative answers a question about a booking
steps.description: A representative takes a call about an existing booking, for example how to prepare for a fasting test, how to find the centre, or a lost confirmation, looks up the appointment and answers or hands the caller on.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Support agent removes a duplicate booking
steps.description: A support agent works through the daily list of patients holding more than one future booking, confirms which one the patient wants from the most recent booking or by text, and cancels the extra slot so others can use it.

error.defect_description: The wrong one of two bookings is cancelled.

evidence.note: Common clean-up practice for self-booking tools; author's estimate.

steps.name: Team lead confirms a special-test slot
steps.description: For a glucose tolerance test, Holter monitor or breath test the representative messages the centre, and the team lead checks that a trained person, the device and a long enough slot are free before the booking is confirmed to the patient.

next.condition: no suitable slot at that centre

evidence.note: Tests that need appointments are booked with the centre (dyn_before); times are estimates.

exceptions.name: No-show
exceptions.description: The patient does not come; the slot is released 15 minutes after the booked time and stays empty unless a walk-in is moved into it.

exceptions.name: Patient cancels or reschedules
exceptions.description: The patient uses the reminder link or phones to move or cancel; a moved booking goes back to slot selection.

exceptions.name: Unexpected centre closure
exceptions.description: Staff shortage, weather or an outage closes a centre; the team lead blocks the schedule and the contact centre contacts every booked patient to rebook.

exceptions.name: Missing confirmation or booking error
exceptions.description: The patient gets an error or no confirmation, often because of a mistyped email or phone number, and digital support fixes the booking the next business day.

exceptions.name: Special test by phone
exceptions.description: A timed or device-based test needs the centre team lead to confirm staff, device and a long slot before the representative confirms the booking.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from booking request to arrival or other end

evidence.note: Author's estimate of booking lead time: most patients book for the next few days and the tool allows up to 4 weeks (dyn_myturn).

benchmarks.population: Company booking tool after the reference period

evidence.note: Up to 4 weeks in advance at participating locations.

benchmarks.population: Company booking tool after the reference period

benchmarks.unit: minutes for 90% of patients after arrival

evidence.note: Average actual waits 14 and 17 minutes.

benchmarks.population: Ten outpatient clinics at a US veterans hospital

evidence.note: Upper reference; laboratory visits booked a few days ahead are assumed to have fewer no-shows.

pain_points.description: No-shows and late cancellations leave booked slots empty while walk-ins wait, which makes it hard to set how many slots to offer.

evidence.note: No-shows are common and reminders reduce them only modestly.

pain_points.description: Unexpected closures force the contact centre to reach every booked patient by phone or text at short notice.

evidence.note: Locations may close unexpectedly.

pain_points.description: Mistyped contact details stop confirmations and reminders, and digital support only answers in office hours, so fixes take about a day.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

pain_points.description: Uploaded requisitions are not linked to the booking, so centre staff must search for them by name at registration.

evidence.note: Patients tell staff on arrival that the requisition was uploaded.

sources.title: MyTurn: join the line, book an appointment or walk in
sources.supports: Current booking tool (after the reference period, powered by WaitWell): appointments up to 4 weeks in advance at participating locations; confirmation text and email with links to reschedule or cancel; notification 10 minutes before the patient's turn; arrive about 10 minutes early and tell the front desk; booked spots held up to 15 minutes past the appointment; pre-booked patients prioritised over walk-ins.

sources.title: Find a location
sources.supports: Location finder with join-the-line and book-an-appointment links, real-time wait updates and a note that some locations may be closed unexpectedly.

sources.title: Before my test
sources.supports: Most visits do not require appointments; appointments are needed for glucose, lactose and xylose tolerance tests, Holter monitoring, urea breath tests, breath alcohol, US DOT urine collections and some Quebec services, booked by contacting the nearest centre; bring a signed requisition and health card; requisition upload tool linked.

sources.title: Upload Ontario lab requisitions conveniently and securely (partner update, September 2020)
sources.supports: From September 2020 physicians and patients can upload Ontario requisitions online; required fields are physician and patient names, date of birth and requisition date; requisitions older than 6 months are not accepted; the patient receives a confirmation email with information on checking in remotely and tells staff on arrival that the requisition was uploaded.

sources.title: Requisition uploader
sources.supports: Upload form with required physician and patient names and date of birth, optional health card number and email, and a file upload control.

sources.title: The consumer health service
sources.supports: Patient portal in Ontario and Quebec that lets patients see results and keep track of their appointments.

sources.title: 2017 Annual Report, Section 3.07: Laboratory Services in the Health Sector
sources.publisher: Office of the Auditor General of Ontario
sources.supports: Community laboratories set their own collection wait targets (90% of patients served within 30 or 40 minutes of arrival); in 2016/17 the two sampled community laboratories averaged 14 and 17 minutes and met their targets for 87% and 89% of patients; wait times were the improvement most often named by patients.

sources.title: Prevalence, predictors and economic consequences of no-shows (Kheirkhah P et al., BMC Health Services Research 16:13)
sources.supports: Mean outpatient no-show rate 18.8% in 10 clinics (12.6% to 25.7%); reminder letters did not change it and a centralised phone reminder system lowered it only modestly.

sources.title: Wages: Customer Service Representative - Call Centre in Ontario (NOC 64409)
sources.supports: Ontario hourly wages low $17.95, median $21.50, high $33.17 (2023-2024).

assumptions: About 90% of bookings are made online and 10% by phone through the contact centre; the organisation file does not give the split.
Patient time spent booking, uploading and travelling is not counted as hands-on time (touch time 0 for patient steps), so the staffing line covers staff only.
The no-show rate is set at 10% of arrivals due and cancellations at 11%, below the 18.8% outpatient clinic rate in kheirkhah2016, because laboratory bookings are usually made a few days ahead.

The MyTurn tool described on the company website is later than 2019 to 2022; its rules (4-week horizon, 15-minute hold, confirmation links) are taken as typical of the booking tool used in the period.

Check-in at the counter is done by the lab assistant and documented in the registration workflow; this workflow ends when the booked patient joins the registration queue. The registration workflow assumes 45% of its visits come from bookings; with 320,000 bookings a month and about 77% attending, this workflow supplies about 245,000 visits, consistent with that share.
Loaded costs come from the organisation file (hourly wage times 1.35).
